text: After Saul’s turning, the assemblies throughout Judea, Galilee and Samaria had peace for a time (Acts 9:31).
One after another they hold up what she made: a child’s coat, a mantle, a tunic let out for a woman who was carrying a child. Every one has been worn thin.
Tanners worked the hides of dead animals. The work was foul-smelling and ritually unclean, and tanneries were kept away from where people lived. Simon’s was by the sea.
A widow holds a coat out toward you without a word.
You wait on the outside stairs with the widows. No one says anything. Through the shutter you hear one man praying.
They have washed her and laid her out in the upper room. The widows of Joppa sit around her, and none of them will leave.
She had a loom and two good hands, and she would not keep either for herself. When my husband died she was at my door before the mourners were.
speaker: A widow

text: You wait at the gate until the light changes. Then you see them on the Lydda road: two men from Joppa, and a big fisherman walking between them.
You come down to the coast with letters for the believers in Joppa. You find them in mourning.
The house smells of lime and hides. Peter does not seem to notice. You notice that he does not notice.
He gave her his hand, and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
Peter put them all out, and kneeled down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.

Peter got up and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper chamber. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them.
It happened, that he stayed many days in Joppa with one Simon, a tanner.
And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated, means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did. It happened in those days that she fell sick, and died. When they had washed her, they laid her in an upper chamber. As Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, imploring him not to delay in coming to them.
